Platinum TKK supported on nickel hydroxide

nodes.name: Pt islands electrodeposition on Pt(111)
nodes.procedure: Pt(111) modified by electrochemically deposited Pt islands (diameters ~1-3 nm, monoatomic height), referred as Pt-islands/Pt(111). After 50 potential cycles between -0.3 V and +0.3 V, the STM images and CV traces remain stable.
nodes.source_text: Pt(111) and Pt(111) modified by electrochemically deposited Pt islands... After 50 potential cycles between -0.3 V and +0.3 V

nodes.name: Ni(OH)₂ electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Ni-(hydr)oxide clusters electrochemically deposited on Pt(111), Pt-islands/Pt(111), Pt(110), and Pt nanoparticles. Clusters exhibit hemisphere-like/ellipsoidal shapes with heights ~0.7-0.8 nm. Ni remains in +2 valence state (XANES/EXAFS confirmed Ni-O: 2.05±0.01 Å, Ni-Ni: 3.08±0.01 Å). Volmer-Weber 3D growth observed.
nodes.source_text: Modified Pt(111) and Pt-island Pt(111) surfaces by depositing Ni-(hydr)oxide clusters (38)... XAS measurements

nodes.name: Li⁺ modification of Ni(OH)₂/Pt
nodes.procedure: Addition of solvated Li⁺ ions into the compact portion of the double layer of Ni(OH)₂/Pt-islands/Pt(111) electrodes in KOH solutions.
nodes.source_text: Further enhancement of water dissociation is achieved by the introduction of solvated Li⁺ ions

nodes.description: HER performance in alkaline solution (0.1 M KOH)
nodes.source_text: HER activities for Pt(111), Pt-islands/Pt(111), and Ni(OH)₂/Pt(111) surfaces in alkaline solution (a, b, and c, respectively)

nodes.description: HER performance in 0.1 M KOH vs acid
nodes.source_text: in alkaline solution, relative to the corresponding pristine Pt(111) surface, the Pt-islands/Pt(111) surface is ∼5 to 6 times as active for the HER. Figure 1D also shows that in acid solution, the HER on the Pt-islands/Pt(111) electrode is improved by a factor of only ∼1.5
the Ni(OH)2/Pt(111) electrode is ∼7 times as active for the HER relative to Pt(111)

nodes.description: HER performance in 0.1 M KOH at 6 mA/cm²
nodes.source_text: the most active Ni(OH)₂/Pt-islands/Pt(111) electrodes in KOH solutions are more active for the HER by a factor of ∼8 at an overpotential of −0.1 V. at 6mA/cm², the difference in overpotential between the HER in alkaline and acid solutions is reduced to only 100mV

nodes.description: HER with Li+ enhancement in 0.1 M KOH at 5 mA/cm²
nodes.source_text: Further enhancement... resulting in a factor of 10 total increase in activity... the HER on Ni(OH)₂/Pt-islands Pt(111) is enhanced by almost a factor of 2 in the presence of Li⁺ cations... at 5mA/cm², the difference in overpotential between acid and alkaline environments is narrowed to only 35mV

nodes.description: HER on Pt(110) system in 0.1 M KOH with Li+ at 10 mA/cm²
nodes.source_text: at 10mA/cm² the overpotential for the HER on Ni(OH)₂/Pt islands/Pt(110) in the presence of Li⁺ is reduced by ∼100mV relative to bare Pt(110). ...this surface exhibits activities ∼40mV less than the activities of Pt(110) recorded in acid solutions at 10mA/cm². The Tafel slopes... lie in the range of 100 to 130mV/decade

nodes.description: HER on Pt/C nanocatalyst with Ni(OH)2 and Li+ in 0.1 M KOH at 10 mA/cm²

current_density_ratio.unit: times vs extended surface at 120 mV

nodes.source_text: at 10mA/cm², the difference in overpotential between a Pt-nano electrode in acid solution and a Li⁺/Ni(OH)₂/Pt-nano interface in alkaline solution narrowed to ∼33mV. Given that at the same overpotential (∼120mV) the current density obtained on the nanocatalysts is ∼8 times the current density on the most active extended surface

nodes.description: HER activity in 0.1 M HClO4 (acid reference)
nodes.source_text: The activity for the unmodified Pt/C surface in 0.1 M HCIO4 is shown for reference.
Incremental improvements in activities for the HER in 0.1 M KOH from the unmodified Pt(110) surface

nodes.name: Pt-islands/Pt(111)
aliases: Pt(111) modified by two-dimensional (2D) Pt ad-islands

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt(111) displays randomly distributed mono-atomic steps and 2D Pt islands with diameters of 1 to 2 nm and monoatomic height.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the image of Pt(111) in Fig. 1A displays the presence of a few randomly distributed mono-atomic steps and 2D Pt islands with diameters of 1 to 2 nm and monoatomic height.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt-islands/Pt(111) shows 2D Pt adatoms with diameters ~1 to 3 nm and height of 1 atomic layer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the STM image of the islands shown in Fig. 1B, however, the Pt adatoms can be clearly resolved as 2D features with diameters of ~1 to 3 nm and a height of 1 atomic layer.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni(OH)2 clusters on Pt(111) are hemisphere-like with diameters of ~8 to 10 nm and heights of ~0.7 nm corresponding to two layers.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the STM image in Fig. 1C clearly shows that the Ni(OH)2 clusters are randomly distributed across the (111) terraces. All Ni(OH)2 clusters exhibited hemisphere-like shapes, with characteristic diameters of ~8 to 10 nm and heights of ~0.7 nm

nodes.characterization_summary: No shift in edge energy observed between HER (-0.1 V) and Hupd (0.1 V) regions for Ni(OH)2 on Pt(111), matching reference Ni(OH)2 spectrum.
nodes.evidence_snippet: No shift in the edge energy in XANES spectra between HER and Hupd regions is observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni-O bond distance of 2.05±0.01 Å and Ni-Ni bond distance of 3.08±0.01 Å determined for Ni(OH)2 clusters.
nodes.evidence_snippet: from the analysis of the x-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) and extended x-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) of the XAS spectra ... we found Ni-O and Ni-Ni bond distances of 2.05±0.01Å and 3.08±0.01Å

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni(OH)2 clusters on Pt-islands/Pt(111) are ellipsoidal with heights ~0.8 nm and diameters 4-12 nm; Pt islands covered by Ni(OH)2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The clusters had approximately constant heights of ~0.8 nm but diameters ranging from 4 to 12 nm. The same STM image, however, revealed no visible presence of 2D Pt islands

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni(OH)2 clusters randomly distributed on inherently rough Pt(110) surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: STM image shows Ni(OH)2 randomly distributed on inherently rough Pt(110).

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt-nano catalysts (TKK) show average particle size of 5 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron micrograph image ... of Ni(OH)2 free Pt-nano catalysts (TKK) with an average particle size of 5 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni(OH)2/Pt-islands/Pt(111) clusters appear ellipsoidal with particle sizes between 4 and 12 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Clusters of Ni(OH)2 in the STM image appear ellipsoidal with particle sizes between 4 and 12 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ surface x-ray crystal truncation rod measurements confirm surface morphologies of Ni(OH)2/Pt(111) and Ni(OH)2/Pt-islands/Pt(111).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The surface morphologies of Ni(OH)2/Pt(111) and Ni(OH)2/Pt-islands/Pt(111) were probed by STM and in situ surface x-ray crystal truncation rod (CTR) measurements
